description:
Location: crate-jmap-filenode-server/src/memory.rs:125-128 (next_node_id) and
crate-jmap-filenode-server/src/memory.rs:196-205 (seed_node).

```rust
fn next_node_id(&mut self) -> Id {
    self.node_counter += 1;
    Id::from(format!("node-{}", self.node_counter))
}
```

```rust
pub fn seed_node(&self, account_id: &str, node: FileNode) {
    let mut guard = self.inner.lock().unwrap();
    if let Some(store) = guard.accounts.get_mut(account_id) {
        store.nodes.insert(node.id.clone(), node);
    }
}
```

The ID-counter and the seed path are unaware of each other. If a
downstream contributor / consumer writes test fixtures with the
natural-looking IDs:

```rust
backend.seed_node("acc1", make_dir("node-1", "fixture-root", None));
```

…and then exercises the create handler, `next_node_id` will emit
`Id::from("node-1")` on the first create call. The `HashMap::insert`
in `create_object` (memory.rs:473) silently overwrites the seeded
fixture. The seeded `fixture-root` node is lost; the test sees a
single node named whatever the handler created. The test result is
not "the seed was lost" — it is a successful-looking create response
plus a subsequent get returning the new node. Debugging the lost
fixture is awkward.

Two compounding factors:

1. `MemoryBackend::seed_node` does NOT bump `node_counter`. Even if
   the seed populates `node-1` ... `node-3` and the counter is at
   0, the next create emits `node-1` and overwrites the seed.
2. The output of `next_node_id` is documented nowhere — the format
   `node-N` is implementation detail. A test author with no reason
   to peek inside memory.rs will pick exactly that format because it
   reads cleanly in tests.

Required fix (choose one):

(a) Document the ID format in `seed_node`'s docstring with a
    warning: "Do not seed IDs of shape `node-N` — those collide
    with the ID counter." Easy but relies on contributor reading
    the docstring.

(b) Have `seed_node` parse the seeded ID for the `node-N` shape and
    bump `node_counter` past it. Easy enough: if id matches
    `^node-([0-9]+)$`, set `node_counter = max(node_counter, N)`.
    Slightly fragile but matches the reference-impl spirit.

(c) Change `next_node_id` to use a less-likely-to-collide prefix
    like `mem-node-N` or a UUID. Best long-term, but a layered
    breaking change to any test that hardcoded expected ids.

P3 hygiene: the trap is real and was demonstrably easy to hit on my
first read of the file, but the fix is a per-file local change and
the production-vs-reference-impl distinction limits blast radius.

LABELS: api-contract, defensive
title: MemoryBackend::next_node_id format collides with externally-seeded node IDs of shape 'node-N'
